metadata.title: TIMSS 1999 Database User Guide – Supplement 2: Documentation of National Adaptations of International Background Questionnaire Items
metadata.venue: IEA (International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This supplement is documentation for the TIMSS 1999 background questionnaires and national adaptations, not an empirical analysis paper. It does not describe any analytic sample selection, scaling, or estimation procedure that would require applying student sampling weights or replicate weights. For secondary analyses using the TIMSS 1999 international database, users should follow the main TIMSS 1999 User Guide for the background questionnaires and the TIMSS technical documentation on complex survey design and weight variables. Because this document focuses on questionnaire item comparability (including which countries’ data are included or excluded for specific items), it does not provide weight variable names or replicate design details.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a questionnaire item documentation supplement rather than an empirical study predicting an outcome from TIMSS student data. It does not generate or analyze cognitive achievement scores with plausible values, and it does not report any missing-data handling strategy for an analytic model. Therefore, PV handling and missing-data handling are not applicable to the supplement’s purpose, and the absence of these methodological details reflects the documentation nature of the text rather than a reporting gap.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This supplement does not define an analytic student sample. Instead, it documents item-level national adaptations and indicates, for each questionnaire item and country, whether the national data are included in the international database (Code D) or not included (Code X), along with notes on comparability and trend status.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 1999 Database User Guide supplement documents how countries adapted international background questionnaire items for the TIMSS 1999 eighth-grade study. It is organized by questionnaire type (student background, mathematics teacher background, science teacher background, and school background) and lists each item with its questionnaire location reference, an abbreviated question, variable names, and links to the 1995 trend counterpart. For each item, the supplement provides a trend status indicator (same question/response options, modified parts, or not administered in 1995) and national adaptation notes by country. Crucially, it also flags whether internationally comparable data are available for secondary analysis: Code D indicates inclusion in the international database, while Code X indicates exclusion due to non-administration, non-comparability, deletion, or other data issues. The document does not report model-based results or performance metrics because it is not an empirical study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a documentation supplement rather than an empirical research article. As such, it does not report an analytic sample size, country-level student counts, plausible-value estimation, missing-data handling, or any machine-learning model training/evaluation. The sparse methodological fields are expected because the document’s function is to support secondary users in assessing item comparability and availability across countries.
